steps.name: Batch-adjusted DESeq2 differential expression
caveats: Verify sample ID column names/order match exactly between counts.csv column headers and metadata.csv rows before constructing colData -- do not assume positional order is correct

Confirm the batch variable is coded as a factor with at least 2 balanced levels within each condition before fitting; if it is not balanced as described, report this discrepancy rather than silently proceeding
Use raw integer counts directly with DESeq2 -- do not pre-normalize or log-transform before DESeq()
Report genes with very low counts across all samples as filtered out if independent filtering removes them, so the top-line summary reflects testable genes
steps.context: Counts file: /eval-sonnet-r2-without-batch-balanced-n6-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 13 columns: 1 gene-symbol column + 12 sample columns). Metadata file: /eval-sonnet-r2-without-batch-balanced-n6-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows x 3 columns: sample, condition, batch). Design is 6 treated vs 6 control with 2 batches balanced across condition, so batch can be safely added as a covariate in the DESeq2 design without confounding the condition effect.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control kidney samples (6 vs 6), controlling for the two known processing batches that are balanced across conditions?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 is run on raw integer counts (counts.csv, 12000 genes x 12 samples after excluding the gene-symbol column) with design formula ~batch + condition
Sample metadata (condition, batch) from metadata.csv is correctly matched to count matrix columns by sample ID before building the DESeqDataSet
Results table reports log2FoldChange, shrunken LFC (via apeglm or ashr), p-value and BH-adjusted p-value (padj) for the treated vs control contrast, for all ~12000 genes
A PCA plot of variance-stabilized (vst) data colored by condition and shaped/labeled by batch is produced to visually confirm batch and condition separation
A summary count of genes at padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1 is reported
Full results table (all genes, not just significant) is saved as a CSV for downstream enrichment

steps.name: WikiPathways enrichment of treated vs control DE genes
caveats: The gmt file mixes descriptor metadata into the first field -- parse it correctly (split on '%') rather than treating the raw first field as the pathway name

Confirm gene identifiers in the DESeq2 results (from counts.csv gene symbol column) are HGNC symbols matching the gmt's gene identifier space; if a large fraction fail to match, report the mismatch rate rather than proceeding silently
If the reference WikiPathways file is unexpectedly absent or empty at run time, report that pathway enrichment could not be performed rather than fabricating results
steps.context: Reference: WikiPathways human pathway gene sets at /mnt/refs/managed/wikipathways-human/2026.07.10/wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt, tab-separated GMT with a '%'-delimited descriptor field (name, WikiPathways ID, species) in column 1 and HGNC gene symbols as members from column 3 onward. Split the descriptor on '%' to recover a readable pathway name before reporting results.
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control kidney samples?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the full DESeq2 results table (all ~12000 genes, log2FoldChange and padj) from T1S1 as input

Runs over-representation analysis (ORA) on genes at padj < 0.05 (or GSEA on the full ranked list by signed statistic, e.g. sign(log2FC)*-log10(pvalue)) against the WikiPathways Homo sapiens gene sets available in the reference store
Reports enriched pathways with adjusted p-values (BH) and the member genes driving each enrichment
If fewer than 5 genes pass the significance threshold for ORA, falls back to GSEA on the full ranked gene list and states this explicitly
Gene symbols in the counts/results table (HGNC-style) are matched directly against the WikiPathways gmt gene symbols; unmatched genes are reported as a count, not silently dropped

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch adjustment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (salmon-derived raw integer counts, 12000 genes x 13 samples incl. gene symbol column) from human kidney tissue, 6 treated vs 6 control, with two known processing batches balanced across conditions. Because batch is fully balanced with respect to condition, it can and should be included as a covariate in the differential expression model rather than requiring more aggressive correction (e.g. ComBat), which risks removing biological signal when the design is already balanced. Step 1 runs DESeq2 with a ~batch+condition design to get robust, batch-adjusted differential expression results plus diagnostic QC (PCA, dispersion) to confirm the batch effect is a real but modest confounder and that the balanced design is adequate. Step 2 takes the resulting significant gene list and ranked statistic and performs pathway enrichment against WikiPathways human gene sets, which are available in the reference store, to place the treated-vs-control transcriptional changes into biological context. This two-step flow (DE with covariate adjustment -> functional enrichment) directly answers 'which genes differ between treated and control' while accounting for the known batch structure, and provides pathway-level interpretation without requiring any translational/clinical extensions not supported by the research question.
